Built for how a real counter runs

Every feature below came out of an actual checkout line, not a feature request board.

01

Real bills, not textbook rounding

Quick-cash suggestions are built from the bills your cashiers actually carry, not round numbers a spreadsheet would guess. In the Philippines, that means real peso notes: ₱50, ₱100, ₱500, ₱1000.

02

Cash, GCash, Maya, or bank transfer

Every payment method your customers already use, on the same till, with the same receipt.

03

Senior Citizen / PWD discounts, done right

RA 9994 and RA 10754 math (VAT removed first, then 20% off what's left) with the name and ID capture the law requires. No manual override, no guessing.

04

Never lose a sale to a bad connection

Every cart is saved the moment it's touched. If the app closes or the signal drops mid-sale, nothing is lost: it queues and syncs the second you're back online.

05

One login, many cashiers

Staff clock in with a name and a PIN: no separate account to create for every employee, no shared password written on a sticky note.

06

An assistant that knows your store

Ask what sold today or what's running low, right from the app, with no separate report to pull.

Not a generic register with a peso sign added

Most POS apps are built once and localized after the fact. MERQ started from a Philippine counter.
